conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: PAGE directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'Comment-text-1 may contain any character in the compile-time computer's coded character set except for control characters as specified in Clause 6, Reference format, rule 3b.' (cite.py --check 7.3.19.3 -> OK §7.3.19.3 1)); §6.1 3b 'The implementor shall specify any control characters that terminate a free-form line...' (cite.py --check 6.1 -> OK §6.1 b)). Permission half verified by probe out/probe/page-directive/p2.cob (free form): comment-text with TAB, Latin-1 letters, CJK, the ASCII punctuation set incl. backslash and < >, and a FORM FEED is accepted and the program runs (OK). Exclusion half: the excluded characters are the ones that TERMINATE a line, and the preprocessor splits lines at CR/LF, so a terminating control character cannot lie inside comment-text-1 by construction — nothing further to diagnose. Side note (not this row's defect): docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no §6.1 rule 3b determination naming the line-terminating control characters (the only control-character determination is A.1-115, line sequential files); that obligation belongs to the §6.1 row. No golden puts non-ASCII or control characters in >>PAGE text, so test-ref is empty. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 directive facility is post-85; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to §7.3.19; COBOL-85 has no >> lines — derived edge, VCR Table 7 row 7.21)
rows.rule-text: Comment-text-1 may contain any character in the compile-time computer's coded character set except for control characters as specified in Clause 6, Reference format, rule 3b.

rows.subject: PAGE directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'If a source listing is being produced, a PAGE directive shall cause page ejection followed by listing of the PAGE directive.' (cite.py --check 7.3.19.4 -> OK §7.3.19.4 2)). COBOL.NET produces no source listing at all: cobol --help offers no listing option and no listing writer exists in src/Cobol.Net.* (grep 'listing' finds only directive-state/catalog mentions); docs/CONFORMANCE.md (recognized-and-ignored directives, ~line 525) records '>>LISTING / >>PAGE (§7.3.18 / §7.3.19) — no source listing is produced, so listing on/off and page ejects are inert'. The rule's condition is never true, so it imposes no obligation — vacuously conforming. Reopens if a listing facility is ever added (page eject, then the directive line listed). The conditional arm is untestable today. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 directive facility is post-85; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to §7.3.19; COBOL-85 has no >> lines — derived edge, VCR Table 7 row 7.21)
rows.rule-text: If a source listing is being produced, a PAGE directive shall cause page ejection followed by listing of the PAGE directive.

rows.subject: PROGRAM-ID paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The COMMON clause may be specified only if the program is contained within another program' (--check 11.10.3 -> OK §11.10.3 4)). MakeUnit: `if (common && parent is null) edition.Error("COBOLNET0887", ... (ISO §11.10.3 SR4))`. Probe probe dir out/probe/program-id-paragraph/sr4.cob (outermost `PROGRAM-ID. SR4OUT IS COMMON.`) -> COBOLNET0887 at --std 85, 2002, 2023; contained COMMON programs compile (gr2 probe). FUNCTION-ID has no COMMON arm in its grammar. No golden/unit test pins COBOLNET0887 (grep of tests/ finds none) -> test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: The COMMON clause may be specified only if the program is contained within another program.

rows.subject: PROGRAM-ID paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'A common program is contained within another program but may be called from programs other than that containing it as stated in 8.4.6' (cite.py --check 11.10.4 -> OK §11.10.4 2)); scope rule §8.4.6.3 2) (--check OK). ResolveVisible rule 3 walks the caller's ancestors and admits a sibling only when sib.Common, excluding the COMMON program itself and its containees unless it is recursive (the §8.4.6.3 2) exception); NestedCallablesOf mirrors it for AS NESTED. Probe probe dir out/probe/program-id-paragraph/gr2.cob at --std 85 and 2023: sibling GR2A calls COMMON GR2C -> 'C' runs; GR2A calls non-COMMON sibling GR2N -> ON EXCEPTION 'N NOT VISIBLE'; non-recursive COMMON GR2C calling itself -> 'SELF NOT VISIBLE'. All match the spec. No spec-derived golden exercises COMMON visibility (pb240_call_operand_screens uses COMMON incidentally) -> test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: The COMMON clause specifies that the program is common. A common program is contained within another program but may be called from programs other than that containing it as stated in 8.4.6, Scope of names.

rows.subject: PROGRAM-ID paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'When an initial program is activated, the data items and file connectors contained in it and any program contained within it are set to their initial states' (--check 11.10.4 -> OK §11.10.4 3)). CallProgram: freshInstance = n.Initial||n.Recursive -> new instance (initial WS), CancelContained(n) on activation, and on return (Active==0) CloseFiles + CancelContained + drop instance (§14.9.18 GR2 implicit CANCEL). Probes: probe dir out/probe/program-id-paragraph/gr3.cob (--std 85/2023) INITIAL GR3I with contained non-initial GR3K, each ADD 1 to a VALUE 0 counter, called twice -> 'I 1 / K 1 / I 1 / K 1' while ordinary GR3L shows 'L 1 / L 2' (last-used control). File-connector half: probe dir out/probe/program-id-paragraph/gr3f.cob, INITIAL program OPEN OUTPUT without CLOSE, called twice -> 'OPEN 00' both times (connector reset, not 41). Both halves verified. The only existing golden that pins this behaviour, conformance:2023/pb154_cancel_cascade, declares OUTER154 INITIAL directly containing INNERA154 RECURSIVE -- a §11.10.3 SR6 violation -- so it is not a conforming program and cannot close the row; test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: The INITIAL clause specifies that the program is initial program. When an initial program is activated, the data items and file connectors contained in it and any program contained within it are set to their initial states.

rows.subject: PROPAGATE directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The default for a compilation group is PROPAGATE OFF.' (cite.py --check 7.3.21.4 -> OK §7.3.21.4 4)). With no directive, an unhandled fatal EC in a called program terminates the run unit (§14.6.13.1.3 GR7, no PROPAGATE ON applicable). Probe gr4.cob (gr2t.cob with the directive removed): observed 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION (fatal)' — the OFF behavior, caller's declarative not entered. Conforms, though only because OFF is the sole behavior the compiler has (see GR-7.3.21.4-1); when the ON state is implemented the default must be pinned by a test. No spec-derived covering test exists (tests/conformance/2014/propagate_directive.cob only proves recognition). || editions (adjudicator): COBOL-2002, 2014, 2023 (§7.3.21 is live in the 2023 text; Annex E.2/E.3 list no 2023 introduction or removal, so it predates 2023; not in COBOL-85 — the §7.3 compiler-directive facility)
rows.rule-text: The default for a compilation group is PROPAGATE OFF.

rows.subject: PROPERTY clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Format: PROPERTY [WITH NO {GET|SET}] [IS FINAL]; WITH and IS are not underlined (optional words), so they may be omitted. Grammar `PROPERTY (WITH? NO (GET | SET))? (IS? FINAL)?` matches it exactly. Probes with the pinned compiler at --std 2023: `PROPERTY WITH NO GET SET` -> COBOL0307 (correct: exactly one of GET/SET); `PROPERTY IS FINAL WITH NO GET` -> COBOL0307 (correct: phrase order is as printed); `PROPERTY NO SET.` (WITH omitted), `PROPERTY WITH NO SET IS FINAL`, `PROPERTY FINAL` all compile and run (probe gr_positive). The binder reads pc.NO()/GET()/SET()/FINAL() directly. cite.py --check 13.18.42.2 "PROPERTY" -> OK (General format). No test covers the FINAL phrase or the WITH-less spelling as a golden, so test-ref is empty. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the PROPERTY clause is part of the OO facility; not in 1985)
rows.rule-text:
┌ ╭ GET ╮ ┐ PROPERTY │ WITH NO ┤ ├ │ [ IS FINAL ] └ ╰ SET ╯ ┘
> > > **Figure notes (PROPERTY clause general format).** `PROPERTY`, `NO`, `GET`, `SET`, and `FINAL` are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `WITH` and `IS` are **not** underlined. The `WITH NO …` phrase is bracketed (optional); when it is specified, the `{ GET / SET }` braces require exactly one of `GET` or `SET` — there are **no** choice indicators here, so `WITH NO GET SET` is not a legal single phrase. The `[ IS FINAL ]` bracket sits outside that group.

rows.subject: Polymorphism
rows.adjudicator-notes: CONTEXT (applies to every 9.3.5.3 row): the seven items define the METHOD RESOLUTION SIGNATURE. The feature that DISTINGUISHES methods by it (overloading) is optional -- cite.py OK 9.3.5.3 7) 'Parametric polymorphism is an optional feature' -- and is NOT claimed (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 5 A.4.10 item 3; refused COBOLNET0822 in OoClassTable.Build, both instance and factory arms). But the signature is consumed by MANDATORY rules: cite.py OK 8.4.6.5 'The methods declared in an object class definition shall have unique method resolution signatures', OK 11.7.3 3) 'If the OVERRIDE phrase is specified, there shall be a method with the same method resolution signature', OK 11.7.3 9) (conformance of an inherited/implemented same-named method). inventory-schema.json derived-verdicts.oo-optional-items-only deliberately EXCLUDES these rows and asks for per-row adjudication, so no selector covers them. COBOL.NET's signature is the degenerate one (the NAME: roster key ExternalizedName) and the remaining components are enforced as SR9 conformance by OoConformance.ValidateOverrideSignatures -> MethodConformanceMismatches -> DescriptionMismatch (COBOLNET0829); for any program that does not overload, a component is conforming iff that comparator rejects every override the component distinguishes. Probes: out/probe/polymorphism/p*.cob, pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023 default. Rule: cite.py OK 9.3.5.3 1) 'The method name'. The name (the externalized name, PB303 roster key) IS the implemented signature: TryAddMethod/TryAddFactoryMethod refuse a second same-named method (COBOLNET0822 -- for identical parameters that is exactly 8.4.6.5's duplicate-signature error; for differing parameters it is the declined overloading), and MarkRoster pairs an override with its base by that key (0838 when OVERRIDE finds no base, 0837 when a same-named base method lacks OVERRIDE per 11.7.3 SR4a). Probe p1 (sub OVERRIDE M, PIC X(4) vs base PIC 9(4)) pairs by name and is rejected 0829. No spec-derived test targets this component as such (conformance:negative/oo-parametric-polymorphism witnesses the overloading decline, not this row). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the OO module, and with it the method resolution signature, is a COBOL-2002 introduction -- Annex D.19.5.4.3 describes parametric polymorphism as part of the OO facility; none before 2002)
